Basic Information

  • Host Institution: Heriot-Watt University
  • Study Level: PhD
  • Duration: 3 years
  • Start Date: September 2026
  • Tuition Fees (International): £20,456 per year
  • Delivery: Full-time, Part-time
  • Location: Edinburgh Campus
  • Official Website: https://www.hw.ac.uk/study/research/construction-management-innovation

Project Overview & Significance

This self-funded PhD programme in Construction Management and Innovation is designed for professionals and scholars aiming to lead the future of the construction industry. The industry is undergoing rapid transformation, driven by digitalisation, sustainability demands, and the need for greater efficiency. This programme provides a platform to research innovative solutions to these challenges. By examining the whole construction lifecycle, from procurement to project handover, candidates can develop new frameworks for managing complex construction projects. The research aims to improve productivity, reduce costs, and enhance the sustainability of the built environment. Heriot-Watt’s strong industry links ensure that research is grounded in real-world relevance, bridging the gap between academic theory and industrial practice.

Research Themes & Objectives

The programme encompasses several key research areas. 'Construction Project Management' focuses on risk, logistics, and stakeholder management. 'ICT in Construction' explores the application of Building Information Modelling (BIM), digital twins, and smart construction technologies. 'People and Organisation' examines labour dynamics, safety, and organisational behaviour. 'Procurement' researches sustainable supply chains and contract models. Finally, 'Sustainability' integrates green building practices and lifecycle assessment. The objective is to produce research that directly informs industry standards and government policy, fostering a more efficient and sustainable construction sector.

Training & Development

Students will develop advanced skills in research methodology, data analysis, and project management. The programme offers opportunities to engage with industry partners through seminars and site visits. The Edinburgh Campus provides a collaborative environment, with access to the latest software and research databases. Graduates will be well-positioned for senior management roles in construction firms, consultancies, and regulatory bodies.

Eligibility & Requirements

Applicants must hold a first-class or upper second-class honours degree and a Master's degree in construction, civil engineering, or a related field. Relevant industry experience is highly valued. As this is a self-funded programme, applicants must secure their own funding for tuition and living expenses. Both full-time and part-time study options are available.

How to Apply & Official Contacts

Interested candidates should prepare a research proposal and apply via the Heriot-Watt University application portal. General enquiries can be directed to study@hw.ac.uk. Further information can be found on the official programme website.
